itemListElement.name: Gojo vs Maccy: clipboard history or a broader Mac utility?

acceptedAnswer.text: They overlap on clipboard history, but Maccy is a dedicated clipboard manager. Gojo is the better fit when clipboard access is only one part of the workspace you want.
Maccy says it keeps the history of copied content so you can navigate, search, and reuse earlier clipboard items. It also says data is stored on your computer.

mainEntity.name: Should I choose Gojo or Maccy for clipboard history?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose Maccy for a specialized, keyboard-first clipboard workflow. Choose Gojo when you want clipboard history alongside media, files, reminders, battery, webcam, and display controls.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Maccy and Gojo together?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Maccy can remain your dedicated clipboard manager while Gojo handles the rest of your notch workspace.

blocks.label: Short answer
blocks.copy: Choose Maccy if you want a focused clipboard-history app with search, keyboard-first use, pinned items, and local storage. Choose Gojo if clipboard history is one of several tools you want to access from a broader notch workspace.

content.s: Maccy is stronger when clipboard history is the job. Its official positioning is keyboard-first search and reuse, with a native, minimal interface and local storage.
Gojo is stronger when clipboard access belongs beside other everyday controls. It puts clipboard history near media, files, windows, calendar, battery, webcam mirror, and display controls.
Use Maccy when you want a dedicated clipboard workflow and Gojo when you want the surrounding notch utilities.

Comparison pages are only useful if they are honest about scope. Gojo is a MacBook notch utility, not a blanket replacement for every specialist app. Before granting macOS Accessibility, Automation, Camera, Calendar, or other permissions to any utility, check whether the requested access matches the feature you plan to use.
